A1.p.purpose: Frame the topic before any search: review type, question framework and slots, search axes, outcomes, timeframe, eligibility criteria, completion criterion
A1.p.when: all depths; first Unit of the topic
reads: files the topic file names, read-only
A1.p.frozen: protocol.topic_sha256 = sha256 of the topic file when A1.p was written

revised_by.via: it_screen.py:cmd_amend (writes `criteria_amendments` in screening_scores.json, rendered beside the criteria; the protocol itself is not edited)

schemas.step0.protocol: ideate-protocol/1: {review_type: scoping, reporting_standard: PRISMA-ScR, purpose, framework {name, rationale, alternative?, slots[{slot, value, operational_role, reason}]}, axes[{id C#, kind search|anchor|contrast|counter|rigor, slot?, outcome?, name, terms[]}], outcomes[{id O#, text}], timeframe, timeframe_reason, setting, criteria {inclusion[{id IN#, text, refs[]}], exclusion[{id EX#, text, refs[]}]}, completion_criterion, topic_sha256, written_at, history[], a1p_note}

A1.p.scratch: _state/A1/protocol.json (the draft the tool reads); writes the view step1_protocol.md (rebuilt from step0, owned by no Unit)

done_when.check: review type scoping, reporting standard PRISMA-ScR, topic / topic_file / depth present
the framework is a known one and its slots are exactly its own (no force-filled PICO); a rationale is given
every slot has a value, an operational role and the searchability-test reason
the anchor slot is searched
2-4 search axes, each tied to a searched slot, each with enough synonyms; terms of 1-4 words without operators
terms carry no Boolean operators or brackets (the tool renders them)
outcomes listed when the frame has an outcome slot; a searched outcome slot has an axis per outcome
>= 1 inclusion and >= 1 exclusion criterion
every outcome is referred to by an inclusion criterion
every eligibility-only slot is applied by a criterion
timeframe YYYY-YYYY with a reason; completion criterion present
the axis kinds the depth needs exist (anchor; contrast from standard; counter at deep)
no protocol key without an owner
a changed topic file is reported STALE (warning)
no step0 key without an owner (warning; shared by every step0 writer)

failures: topic file unreadable
the frame does not fit the question (caught by A1.e)
A1.p.resume: skip-if-done: protocol present and `frame check --unit A1.p` passes; a changed topic file is reported STALE and re-run on request
A1.p.status_line: A1.p ✔ PICO · 2 search axes (7 terms) · O×2 · IN 3 / EX 2 · 2013–2026
decisions: what counts as this topic
which question framework
which concepts are searched and in which words
the eligibility criteria
the timeframe
A1.p.provenance: every slot carries its searchability reason; every criterion names the slots and outcomes it applies
A1.p.override: a revised protocol through `frame set-protocol --note <reason>`; after the search a synonym through A2.c's `frame add-terms`, an ambiguous term retired through A2.c's `frame retire-terms`

A1.q.purpose: Turn the axes into query variants (Boolean + flat), name anchor terms, sources and known items, and probe the scope
A1.q.instance: per topic (later changes are A2.c revisions, not new instances)
A1.q.when: all depths; the scope probe from standard
A1.q.frozen: strategy_basis.protocol_sha = the protocol it was built on (Q21); scope_probe.strategy_sha = the strategy the probe answered (Q20)

schemas.step0.queries[]: {id, strategy primary|synonym-swap|loosen|anchor-methods|contrast|counter-evidence|recent|rigor, axes {C#: "all" | [terms]}, flat_query, rationale, year?, status active|retired, boolean_query (rendered), query (= flat_query)}
schemas.step0.scope_probe: {at, limit, queries[{id, flat_query, hits_per_source, openalex_total}], rough_yield, known_items[{ref, resolved, title, doi, year}]} | {at, skipped}

A1.q.scratch: _state/A1/strategy.json (draft); _state/probes/A1q/ (probe answers, never in the collection); _mcp_scholar.log (the scholar server's log, appended and credential-scrubbed; shared with A2.s and A5); writes the view step1_protocol.md (rebuilt from step0, owned by no Unit)

exactly one active primary

>= 2 known sources

counts: known items found by the probe

decisions: which variants and which words ask the databases
which sources
what an on-topic paper must contain (anchor terms)
which papers the search must find (known items)

A1.e.purpose: An independent reader evaluates the protocol and the strategy before any search (Kitchenham §5.5)
A1.e.instance: per topic; round 1, and round 2 after one forced revision
reads: step1_protocol.md (the rendered view) - nothing else; the brief names only these paths
forbidden: everything else in the research folder
A1.e.frozen: rounds[].protocol_sha = the protocol and the queries as A1.q wrote them; A2.c's declared revisions after the search do not make it stale

a failed check carries severity and fix target

which component must change

A2.s.purpose: Run each query (and the dense instance) against its sources in the form each source parses, and record every attempt
A2.s.instance: per query (id + rendering hash); D1 = the dense instance; a re-run with another rendering is a new instance
A2.s.when: all depths; D1 at standard and deep
A2.s.frozen: the instance hash = sha of the per-source rendering, year window and limit

A2.s.network: scholar (PubMed, Scopus, IEEE, WoS, OpenAlex, arXiv, Semantic Scholar) + S2 recommendations
A2.s.budget: about 30-60 s per query plus waits; no model tokens
A2.s.scratch: _state/net/scholar/ (recorded answers); _mcp_scholar.log (the server's log, credential-scrubbed; shared with A1.q and A5)
